items.title: Definition 3.1.1 (preprint 3.1): sc-germs of neighbourhoods

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.1 (preprint 3.1), p. 89 (preprint p. 62)
book.statement: An sc-germ of neighbourhoods $\mathcal O(C, 0)$ around $0$ in a partial quadrant $C \subseteq E$ is a decreasing sequence $U_0 \supset U_1 \supset \cdots$ with $U_m$ a relatively open neighbourhood of $0$ in $C_m = C \cap E_m$; its tangent $T\mathcal O(C, 0)$ is $U_1 \oplus E_0 \supset U_2 \oplus E_1 \supset \cdots$. A relatively open $U \ni 0$ with $U_m = U \cap E_m$ is an example; \"the size of the sets $U_m$ does not matter\".

lean.statement: An `ScNbhdGerm E C` is a family of sets $U_m \subseteq E_m$, each of the form $O \cap C_m$ with $O$ open and $0 \in U_m$, nested along the inclusions $E_{m+1} \to E_m$. Its tangent germ has levels $U_{m+1} \times E_m$; `ofSet` is the text's example $U_m = U \cap E_m$. The theorems on germs ask $C$ to be *quadrant-like* (every $C_m$ convex with nonempty interior, $0 \in C$), which every partial quadrant is; then derivatives on $U_1$ are unique.

chips: a germ is a fixed sequence of sets
diff: A germ is a fixed sequence of sets, not a class \"up to shrinking\". items.title: Definition 3.1.2 (preprint 3.2): sc$^k$-germs

lean.statement: `IsSc0Germ`, `IsSc1GermWith` (with a given derivative family), `IsSc1Germ`, `IsSckGerm`, `IsScSmoothGerm` are the notions of Definitions 1.1.13–1.1.15 and of the unnumbered definition after them (preprint Definitions 1.12–1.15) with $U \cap E_m$ replaced by $U_m$. items.title: The calculus of germs

items.title: Definition 3.1.3 (preprint 3.3): sc-smooth section germs

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.3 (preprint 3.3), p. 91 (preprint p. 63)
book.statement: An sc-smooth section germ $(f, x_0)$ of $P : Y \to X$ is a continuous section $f : V \to P^{-1}(V)$ near the smooth point $x_0$ such that in a strong bundle chart with $\varphi(x_0) = 0$ the principal part $\mathbf f$ of $\Phi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1} : O \to K$ has $\mathbf f \circ r : \mathcal O(C, 0) \to F$ an sc-smooth germ.

lean.statement: `StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSectionGerm f x₀`: $x_0$ smooth, and for some strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas (`StrongBundle.IsChart`) with $\varphi(x_0) = 0$, $\mathbf f \circ r$ is an sc-smooth germ on some sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$ with $G_0 \subseteq U$, whose levels may shrink with $m$ (the text’s germ reading). An sc-smooth section is an sc-smooth section germ at every smooth point with a centred chart (with the germ $U \cap E_m$).

diff: \"A strong bundle chart\" is read as a chart compatible with the atlas, not a member of it: a chart of the atlas need not be centred at $x_0$, and the notion must not depend on the atlas within its class (Findings, Chapter 3, item 41). That it does not is proved: equivalent atlases have the same compatible charts (`isChart_congr`; V2.58, Findings, Chapter 2, item 43). Updated in the third addendum of this page.
Continuity of $f$ near $x_0$ is not a separate field: it follows near $x_0$ from the continuity of $\mathbf f \circ r$ on level $0$ of the germ.

**Germs.** Since the fourth addendum of this page the definition is in the text’s germ reading: $\mathbf f \circ r$ is an sc-smooth germ on some sc-germ of neighbourhoods inside $U$, whose levels may shrink with $m$, as for Definitions 3.1.4, 3.1.6 and 3.1.11 (preprint 3.4, 3.6 and 3.11) since phase 2. Before, it was required on the whole $U$ of the chart (levels $U \cap E_m$), which is stricter: a function $C^k$ on $(-1/k, 1/k)$ for every $k$ is an sc-smooth germ in the constant scale $\mathbb R$ and sc-smooth on no neighbourhood of $0$ (`exists_isScSmoothGerm_not_isScSmooth`). No theorem assumes the definition. Hence “hypotheses explicit” again (“narrower” from the third addendum until the fourth) (Findings, Chapter 3, items 220–221, 260; round-trip item V3.5).

items.title: The section algebra and the sum rule

book.label: §3.1, used in Theorems 3.1.13, 3.1.18 (preprint 3.12, 3.15) ("$f + s$ is an sc-smooth section"), p. 98 (preprint p. 71)
book.statement: Not stated: the fibrewise sum of sections, principal parts in a chart, the sum rule of the sc-calculus, and the sc-smoothness of the local representatives of sc$^+$-sections in a chart that is not in the atlas.

lean.statement: The fibrewise sum $f + s$ is a section with principal part $\mathbf f + \mathbf s$ in every chart; $f(x) = 0$ iff $\mathbf f(\varphi(x)) = 0$; the fibres of $K$ are linear. Sums, differences and negatives of sc-smooth maps on relatively open subsets of partial quadrants are sc-smooth. In every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas, $z \mapsto (z, \mathbf f(z))$ is sc-smooth $O \to K$ for an sc-smooth section and $z \mapsto (z, \mathbf s_1(z))$ is sc-smooth $O \to K[1]$ for an sc$^+$-section.

items.title: Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4): fillers

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4), p. 91 (preprint p. 64)
book.statement: For a tame strong local bundle $K = R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$, $R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)$, $r(0) = 0$, an sc-smooth section germ $(f, 0)$ has a filling $(g, 0)$ (an sc-smooth section germ of $U \triangleleft F \to U$) if (1) $f = g$ on $O$ near $0$; (2) $g(y) = \rho(r(y))g(y)$ for $y \in U$ near $0$ forces $y \in O$; (3) the linearization of $y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ at $0$, restricted to $\ker Dr(0)$, is a topological isomorphism onto $\ker\rho(0)$.

lean.statement: `IsFillingGerm` for the principal parts $f, g : E_0 \to F_0$ (the text’s germ reading, also Definition 3.1.6 (preprint 3.6), V3.9): $g$ is an sc-smooth germ on an sc-germ of neighbourhoods $G$ with $G_0 \subseteq U$; (1) and (2) near $0$; (3) the map $y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)$ (`fillDefect`) is an sc$^1$-germ on $G$ with a derivative family $Dk$, and $Dk(0)$ induces a continuous linear equivalence $\ker Dr(0) \simeq \ker\rho(0)$. Here $r(u) = (R(u, 0))_1$, $\rho(u)h = (R(u, h))_2$, with $R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)$, $r \circ r = r$, $\rho(x)$ a projection for $x \in O$, and $\rho(u)$ a bounded operator. The whole-chart form `IsFillerOf` asks the map in (3) to be sc$^1$ on all of $U$ and says nothing about the regularity of $g$.

items.title: Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5): the filler and the linearization

book.label: §3.1, the paragraph after Definition 3.1.4 (preprint 3.4) and Proposition 3.1.5 (preprint 3.5), pp. 91–93 (preprint pp. 64–65)
book.statement: If $f$ has the filling $g$ and $f(0) = 0$, then in the splittings $E = Dr(0)E \oplus \ker Dr(0)$, $F = \rho(0)F \oplus \ker\rho(0)$, $Dg(0) = \begin{pmatrix} Tf(0) & * \\ 0 & C \end{pmatrix}$ with $C$ an isomorphism, and (1) $Tf(0) : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is onto iff $Dg(0)$ is; (2) $Tf(0)$ is Fredholm iff $Dg(0)$ is, with equal index.

lean.statement: For a filler $g$ of $f$ with $g$ sc-smooth, $g(0) = 0$ and $f$ a section of $K \to O$: $D(\rho(r(\cdot))g)(0) = \rho(0)Dg(0)$, $(1 - \rho(0))Dg(0)Dr(0) = 0$, $D(f \circ r)(0) = Dg(0)Dr(0)$; and $Tf(0) := Dg(0)|_{Dr(0)E} : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is onto iff $Dg(0)$ is, Fredholm iff $Dg(0)$ is, and $\mathrm{ind}\,Tf(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0)$. The linear algebra holds for any idempotents $p, q$ and $L$ with $(1 - q)Lp = 0$ and $(1 - q)L : \ker p \to \ker q$ a topological isomorphism. In sc form: if $Dg(0)$ is an sc-Fredholm sc-operator, then $Dr(0)E$, $\rho(0)F$, $\ker Dr(0)$ and $\ker\rho(0)$ are sc-subspaces, $Tf(0) : Dr(0)E \to \rho(0)F$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0)$ on every level, and $(1 - \rho(0))Dg(0) : \ker Dr(0) \to \ker\rho(0)$ is an sc-isomorphism (condition (3) of the filler on every level). Conversely, for $Dg(0)$ an sc-operator: $Dg(0)$ is sc-Fredholm if and only if $Tf(0)$ is sc-Fredholm and condition (3) holds on every level. The same for a filling germ (V3.7), with $Dg(0)$ the value at $0$ of any derivative family of $g$ on any germ (`IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5`, `IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5_sc`, `IsFillingGerm.proposition_3_1_5_sc_iff`).

items.title: Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7): basic germs

book.label: §3.1, Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7), p. 94 (preprint p. 66)
book.statement: A basic germ is an sc-smooth germ $f : \mathcal O([0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k} \oplus W, 0) \to \mathbb R^N \oplus W$ with $f(0) = 0$ and $P_W \circ f(a, w) = w - B(a, w)$, $B(0, 0) = 0$, $|B(a, w) - B(a, w')|_m \le \varepsilon|w - w'|_m$ for $(a, w), (a, w')$ close enough to $(0, 0)$ on level $m$, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, $m \ge 0$.

items.title: Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9): the fibre derivative of $B$ is small

book.statement: For $B$ as in Definition 3.1.7 (preprint 3.7), every $\varepsilon > 0$ and $m \ge 0$: $|D_2B(a, w)\zeta|_m \le \varepsilon|\zeta|_m$ for $\zeta \in W_m$ if $(a, w) \in E_{m+1}$ is close enough to $(0, 0)$ in $E_m$; in particular $D_2B(0, 0) = 0$.

items.title: Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11): sc-Fredholm germs

book.statement: $(f, x_0)$ is an sc-Fredholm germ if it has a filled version $(g, 0)$ and a local sc$^+$-section $s$ with $s(0) = g(0)$ such that $g - s$ is conjugated to a basic germ: a strong bundle isomorphism $\Psi : U \triangleleft F \to U' \triangleleft F'$ covering an sc-diffeomorphism $\psi$ with $\Psi \circ (g - s) \circ \psi^{-1}$ a basic germ.

items.title: Theorem 3.1.13 (preprint 3.12): local compactness for sc-Fredholm germs

book.statement: Let $f$ be an sc-smooth section of the tame strong bundle $P : Y \to X$ and $(f, x_0)$ an sc-Fredholm germ with $f(x_0) = 0$. items.title: Definition 3.1.16 (preprint 3.14): sc-Fredholm sections

items.title: Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31): the contraction germ $f^{(1)}$

book.label: §3.3, Lemma 3.3.4 (preprint 3.31), pp. 111 ff. (preprint pp. 86–87)
book.statement: If $f = w - B(a, w)$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^k$, $k \ge 1$, with solution germ $\delta$ of class sc$^j$, then $f^{(1)}(v, b, u, w) = (u - B(v, u), w - DB(v, \delta(v))(b, w))$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ of class sc$^{\min(k-1, j)}$ with solution germ $T\delta$ (\"from the uniqueness\").

lean.statement: If $B$ is sc$^{k+1}$ and $\delta$ is sc$^j$ on $\mathrm{germ}(s) = (N(m+s) \cap \widetilde C)_m$, then $f^{(1)}$, in working form with parameter space $P \times P \supseteq \widetilde C \times P$, fibre $TW$ and regions $N(m+2+s) \times P$, $O(m+1) \times W_m$, $K(m+1) \times W_m$, is a contraction germ of class sc$^{\min(k, j)}$ whose solution germ is $T\delta(v, b) = (\delta(v), D\delta(v)b)$ on $(N(2+s) \cap \widetilde C) \times P$. Its map is $(\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ TB \circ \sigma, \mathrm{pr}_2 \circ TB \circ \Gamma)$ with $\sigma$ a reshuffle and $\Gamma(v, b, u, w) = ((v, \delta(v)), (b, w))$. If the working form also satisfies Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) (as the one built from an sc$^0$-contraction germ does) and $B$ is sc$^1$, then $f^{(1)}$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ in the sense of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) on its germ, for every $s$: an $\varepsilon$-contraction near $0$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$ on every level.

diff: Uniqueness holds only in the contraction region, which must contain $T\delta(v, b)$ for every $b$: the regions are unbounded in $b$, $w$ (Findings, Chapter 3, item 3). \"As one verifies by comparing $Tf$ with $f^{(1)}$\" is the chain rule for germs with the shifted solution germ $v \mapsto \delta(v) \in W_1$ (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs, item 4). The parameter region $N(2+s)$ comes from $D\delta(v)$ needing $v \in N(2)$.

The text's “$f^{(1)}$ is an sc$^0$-contraction germ” in the sense of Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) is proved separately (`isSc0ContractionGerm_next`): on level $m$ its first component is Definition 3.3.1 (preprint 3.28) for $B$ on level $m + 1$, its second needs Lemma 3.1.9 (preprint 3.9) on level $m$ with any $\varepsilon$ (V3.11). The working form records only a $\tfrac12$-contraction on the explicit regions, which is all the proof of Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33) uses (Findings, Chapter 3, item 252). lean.statement: For an sc-Banach space $W$, the constant retraction $c : (a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)$ of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ of $\mathbb R \oplus W$ (sc-smooth, with retract $\{(1, 0)\}$), and every sc-smooth retraction $r$ of a nonempty relatively open $U$ in a partial quadrant $C$: the product retraction $c \times r$, with retract $\{(1, 0)\} \times r(U)$, is not tame. diff: The retraction-level half of the argument that the hypothesis under which the theorems of §3.6 were first proved, “the base retraction of every compatible strong bundle chart is tame”, fails for every strong bundle over a nonempty base: from a compatible chart $(\varphi, U, R, \Phi)$, the chart $(1, \varphi)$ onto $\{1\} \times O$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ (the retraction above with $W = 0$) has the transition maps of the first composed with affine maps, hence is compatible with every chart the first one is. In the chart of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) centred at the zero, $T_0O = Dr(0)E$ and $K_0 = \rho(0)F$ are sc-subspaces and $Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0$ is sc-Fredholm, of index $n - N$ on every level for every conjugating basic germ; in **every** strong bundle chart around a zero $y$, at the point $z$ over $y$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, the levels being transported between charts at smooth points. notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) with the text's hypotheses: surjectivity of $f'(y)$ at the nearby zeros
notFormalized.label: §3.6, Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54), pp. 136–139 (preprint pp. 111–114)
notFormalized.book: (1) At every zero $y$ near $x$ the germ $(f, y)$ is in good position, “from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55”; (2) the solution set near $x$ is a sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a manifold with boundary with corners.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (V3.93, V3.94): with the text's hypotheses (tame germ data, good position in a tame chart, V3.103), every zero $y$ near $x_0$ is in good position in a tame chart, in particular $f'(y)$ is onto. The text's argument does not give the surjectivity (it gives that of the filled linearization only; the same step is in the book's arXiv version); it is proved by an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero for $g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))\lambda$, with Theorem 3.3.3 (preprint 3.30) at the centre for a contraction germ whose regions in $a$ do not depend on $\lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 3, items 180–189). The first form under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (V3.82) is kept; that condition follows from good position (V3.102). (2) is proved from (1) (V3.85, V3.94); the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19): the dimension is the index; $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$; good position for $d_X \equiv 0$
notFormalized.label: §3.1, Theorem 3.1.22 (preprint 3.19), p. 100 (preprint p. 74)
notFormalized.book: The solution set near $x_0$ is a manifold whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index of $f'(x_0)$; at its points $\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)$; and for $d_X(x) = 0$ good position is the surjectivity of $f'(x)$.
notFormalized.instead: **Formalized since the first edition of this page** (second addendum). The dimension: the dimension $d$ of the solution set near a zero in good position is $\dim\ker f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)$ at every zero $y$ near it, in every chart (V3.97, with V3.96), also in Theorems 3.1.26, 3.6.11 (preprint 3.23, 3.57), and the index is locally constant along the solution set (V3.98). The kernel: $D\psi$ maps $\ker f'(y)$, read in the chart at $x_0$, onto the tangent space of the solution graph (V3.99); $T_yS$ as a subspace of $T_yX$ is not formalized (Chapter 2 gap G.13). Good position in a tame chart at $d_X(y) = 0$ is surjectivity, for tame germ data (V3.100), so Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.6.10 (preprint 3.19 and 3.56) hold with “$f'(x)$ surjective” (V3.101). notFormalized.title: The 2021 (untamed) sc-Fredholm germs: tame fillings, and Theorem 3.6.8 for untamed data
notFormalized.label: §3.1 and §3.6, Definitions 3.1.4, 3.6.1 and Theorem 3.6.8, pp. 91, 134–138; with Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27, Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11
notFormalized.book: The 2021 filling asks only for an sc-smooth retraction (no tameness). Theorem 3.6.8 describes the solution set near a zero in good position; its proof (p. 138) uses that the retract is tame. Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26, Corollary 3.1.27 and Theorems 3.6.10, 3.6.11 rest on it.
notFormalized.instead: **Settled** (2026-11-12; V3.130, V3.131): read with the 2021 definitions as printed, Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it. A tame strong bundle over $O \cong \mathbb R$ with an sc-Fredholm section in the 2021 sense has a zero in good position whose solution set is a closed half-line, not a sub-M-polyfold (`theorem_3_6_8_untamed_not`; `theorem_3_1_22_untamed_not` for Theorems 3.1.22, 3.1.26); at that zero the germ has no tame germ data (`not_isScFredholmGermTame_sec_zero`) and is not a 2017 germ (`isScFredholmGerm2021_not_2017`). Corrected form: germ data in a tame chart, the wording of the 2017 text and the preprint and the chart the 2021 proof takes (p. 137): V3.85, V3.94, V3.103; germ data in a chart centred at an interior point of its quadrant are tame (`isScFredholmGermTame_of_chart_interior`). Earlier text of this entry: **Open.** Whether every 2021 sc-Fredholm germ has germ data in a tame chart (Findings, Chapter 3, item 353), and Theorem 3.6.8 and the results resting on it for untamed germ data, are not formalized. The proof step on p. 138 does not go through without a tame chart (V3.115). These theorems are verified with tame germ data (V3.85, V3.94, V3.103); the 2021 corollaries whose proofs do not use tameness are V3.111–V3.114. (2026-11-09) **In part.** Germ data in a compatible chart centred at a point of the interior of its partial quadrant, $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) = 0$, give tame germ data: the chart shrunk into the interior is tame and carries the restricted data (`isScFredholmGermTame_of_chart_interior`, `IsScFredholmGermInterior`); so a 2021 sc-Fredholm section with such germ data at every smooth point has tame germ data (`isScFredholmSectionTame_of_interior`), and Theorem 3.6.8 and the results resting on it hold for it; the hypothesis is satisfiable (`isScFredholmGermInterior_graphSection`). **Open**: germ data in a chart with $d_C(\varphi(x_0)) \ge 1$, which includes every point of $\partial X$ and corner charts at interior points of $X$ (`CornerFilling.zero_not_mem_interior`). **The reading.** Germ data in a tame chart is the wording of Definition 3.6.3 in the preprint (3.50) and in the 2017 text (“a tame strong local bundle”); the 2021 Definition 3.6.3 says “strong local bundle”, and the 2021 theorems' “tame strong bundle” is not defined in the 2021 text, which defines a tame strong bundle retraction (p. 65). For the 2021 text the tame reading is therefore our reading of that phrase (V3.103; Findings, Chapter 3, item 382). (2026-11-12) A local model with untamed germ data is formalized: an sc-smooth family of projections whose rank jumps (`Jump.family`, `Jump.Family.isScSmooth_map`, V3.129) gives a 2021 filling over a non-tame retraction, conjugated to a basic germ and in good position (`UntamedCorner.isFilling2021_g`, `UntamedCorner.isConjugateToBasicGerm_g`, `UntamedCorner.isGoodPositionAtGerm_g`), whose solution set is computed (`UntamedCorner.solutionSet_eq`, `UntamedCorner.theorem_3_6_8_untamed_local`).
